cues.en: So, Tyler's talk is deconstructing the database.
cues.zh: 那么，Tyler 的演讲是在解构数据库。

cues.en: And what
cues.zh: 那么它

cues.en: it is, is it's a look at a new way to look at database architectures.
cues.zh: 实际上是在探讨一种看待数据库架构的新方式。

cues.en: It happens to also be a look at
cues.zh: 它还顺带展示了

cues.en: the underpinnings of the architecture of Datomic, which is a database I've been working on for the last two years.
cues.zh: Datomic 架构的底层基础——这是我过去两年一直在开发的数据库。

cues.en: But it's not a sales pitch for Datomic, it's really about the ideas underlying
cues.zh: 但这不是在推销 Datomic，它真正讲的是这些设计选择背后的

cues.en: the design choices.
cues.zh: 理念。

cues.en: So why do we want to deconstruct the database? What are we trying to accomplish? What problem are we trying to solve?
cues.zh: 那么，为什么要解构数据库？我们想达成什么？要解决什么问题？

cues.en: And I think the fundamental problem we're trying to solve is the
cues.zh: 我认为我们要解决的根本问题，是

cues.en: problem of complexity
cues.zh: 复杂性问题

cues.en: in programming. I mean, how many people think dealing with databases is easy and trouble free?
cues.zh: 在编程中的复杂性问题。我的意思是，有多少人觉得处理数据库轻松无烦恼？

cues.en: Nice.
cues.zh: 不错。

cues.en: Most people don't.
cues.zh: 大多数人并不这么觉得。

cues.en: And there's a number of sources of complexity.
cues.zh: 复杂性的来源有很多。

cues.en: There's this great paper out of the tar pit,
cues.zh: 有一篇很棒的论文，叫 Out of the Tar Pit，

cues.en: and in it the author has sort of identified a bunch of problems,
cues.zh: 论文里，作者大致指出了一堆问题，

cues.en: related to complexity
cues.zh: 它们都与复杂性有关，

cues.en: in programming and they basically said that all complexity boils down to two flavors.
cues.zh: 也就是编程中的复杂性。他们基本认为，所有复杂性都可归结为两类。

cues.en: One
cues.zh: 一类

cues.en: has to do with state, and the other has to do with control.
cues.zh: 与状态有关，另一类与控制有关。

cues.en: And the authors didn't implement it but they suggested that
cues.zh: 作者没有实现它，但他们提出

cues.en: by adopting functional programming and declarative programming
cues.zh: 通过采用函数式编程和声明式编程

cues.en: and a relational model for data inside our applications,
cues.zh: 以及在应用内部采用关系模型来组织数据，

cues.en: we could get rid of this complexity.
cues.zh: 我们就能摆脱这种复杂性。

cues.en: But the... And it's a great paper, I really recommend you read it. But one of the problems with the paper is that
cues.zh: 不过……这是一篇很棒的论文，我强烈推荐你读。但论文的问题之一是，

cues.en: while they had a good grip on the functional programming and declarative programming part,
cues.zh: 虽然他们很好地把握了函数式编程和声明式编程这部分，

cues.en: and also possibly on
cues.zh: 也可能把握了

cues.en: using
cues.zh: 使用

cues.en: a relational model for data inside your applications.
cues.zh: 应用内部的关系模型来组织数据。

cues.en: They really sort of punted, everybody's seen the cartoon where the mathematician has this chalkboard and it's full of full of stuff and then in the bottom corner it says, and then a miracle occurs, right? And then there's the answer.
cues.zh: 他们其实有点回避了这个问题，大家都见过那幅漫画：数学家站在黑板前，黑板上写满了东西，然后角落里写着“然后奇迹发生了”，对吧？接着就给出答案了。

cues.en: And the big thing that was missing from their picture of the world was they imagined there would be this relational model
cues.zh: 他们世界观里缺失的一大块，是设想会有这样一种关系模型

cues.en: of your data that you could access in your application, And that somehow it got updated.
cues.zh: 你的数据可以在应用里访问，而且不知怎么地就被更新了。

cues.en: Like somehow. Something happened in the world and it was different.
cues.zh: 就像不知怎么地，世界上发生了某件事，然后就变了。

cues.en: That all the ick related to state had to do with however that got updated. But it didn't say how it would.
cues.zh: 所有跟状态有关的麻烦都源于它是怎么被更新的。但没说明会怎么更新。

cues.en: And I would call that updating,
cues.zh: 我把这个叫做更新，

cues.en: and the problem that they avoided talking about really, the problem of process in our programs. In other words, we know there's going to be novelty in the world that our programs are going to encounter,
cues.zh: 而他们真正回避不谈的问题，是我们程序中的过程问题。换句话说，我们知道程序会遇到世界上的新事物，

cues.en: where does that go in a model that's otherwise functional,
cues.zh: 在一个本来是函数式的模型里，这该放在哪里，

cues.en: right, or
cues.zh: 对吧，或者

cues.en: as functional as we could make it?
cues.zh: 尽可能做到函数式？

cues.en: So some of the things, some of the other problems we're trying to solve are things we want to obtain
cues.zh: 所以我们要解决的一些问题，是我们想要获得的

cues.en: in
cues.zh: 在

cues.en: looking at the database in a fresh way, I think, is to embrace declarative programming. I agree with the paper, we want declarative programming. What's the best example of declarative programming we encounter most often
cues.zh: 以全新方式看待数据库时，我认为要拥抱声明式编程。我同意那篇论文，我们想要声明式编程。我们最常遇到的最好的声明式编程例子是什么

cues.en: if we're not artificial intelligence researchers?
cues.zh: 如果我们不是人工智能研究者的话？

cues.en: Sequel, actually, is the most declarative thing most of us encounter on a day to day basis.
cues.zh: Sequel 其实是我们大多数人日常接触到的最具声明性的东西。

cues.en: And it ends up that declarative programming
cues.zh: 结果发现，声明式编程

cues.en: is much better at manipulating data than what we do in our languages, even functional languages.
cues.zh: 在处理数据方面，比我们语言里的做法好得多，哪怕是函数式语言。

cues.en: Right? In our languages we sort of go through stuff, we do not have this very nice higher order set logic for dealing with data. And it is superior
cues.zh: 对吧？在我们的语言里，我们得遍历这些东西，没有这种非常优雅的高阶集合逻辑来处理数据。而且它更胜一筹，

cues.en: to dealing with data even in a functional language and way superior
cues.zh: 哪怕在函数式语言里处理数据也更胜一筹，而且远远优于

cues.en: than dealing with data in an object oriented language. We use object oriented languages because we have them, not because they're better at this, they really are much worse at this.
cues.zh: 在面向对象语言里处理数据。我们用面向对象语言只是因为我们有它们，并不是因为它们在这方面更好，它们在这方面其实差得多。

cues.en: One of the problems we have is with a client server database that declarative programming is something that's alien to us, it's sort of over there.
cues.zh: 我们遇到的问题之一，是面对客户端服务器数据库时，声明式编程对我们来说很陌生，它好像在别处。

cues.en: The other problem related to the model these guys were espousing is that there's no basis, right,
cues.zh: 另一个问题跟这些人鼓吹的模型有关，就是没有可以依赖的基础，对吧，

cues.en: that you could rely on. In other words, if I want to do,
cues.zh: 没有你可以依赖的东西。换句话说，如果我想做，

cues.en: I want to calculate something related to a database, what's the basis for that calculation?
cues.zh: 我想计算某个跟数据库相关的东西，那个计算的基础是什么？

cues.en: Well if the whole database is sort of changing all the time, we're back to the problems I talked about in the keynote, right? The database in its entirety is a place,
cues.zh: 如果整个数据库一直在变，那我们就又回到我在主题演讲里谈过的问题了，对吧？整个数据库是一个地方，

cues.en: and we have a problem of saying what's the basis for our decision making? Well I don't know, it was whatever I saw last Tuesday when I ran this computation, but I can't tell you now what that was exactly.
cues.zh: 我们就面临一个问题：我们做决策的基础是什么？嗯，我不知道，就是我上周二跑这个计算时看到的那些，但我现在没法准确告诉你那到底是什么。

cues.en: There are problems with databases related simply to the client server nature,
cues.zh: 数据库存在一些问题，仅仅是因为其客户端-服务器的本质架构，

cues.en: about them being over there. The basis problem is one of them.
cues.zh: 也就是因为它们部署在远端。基准问题就是其中之一。

cues.en: The other is our fear of round trips.
cues.zh: 另一个则是我们对网络往返的恐惧。

cues.en: And we're
cues.zh: 而我们

cues.en: afraid of round trips I think most often for performance reasons.
cues.zh: 害怕网络往返，我认为最主要还是出于性能原因。

cues.en: But actually the biggest round trip problem is that same basis problem.
cues.zh: 但实际上，往返通信最大的问题还是那个基准问题。

cues.en: Right? What if I have a composite decision to make? Can I ask the database three independent questions over time and then get my answer?
cues.zh: 对吧？如果我要做一个复合决策该怎么办？我能随着时间推移向数据库问三个独立的问题，然后得出答案吗？

cues.en: No.
cues.zh: 不行。

cues.en: Why not? Because stuff has happened to that place in between those calls. And it makes us do weird stuff. In particular, one of the things I think it makes us do is couple questions with reporting, right? So let's say you have your application and your application makes a decision about what entities we're going to put on sale or display on this webpage.
cues.zh: 为什么不行？因为在这些调用之间，那个地方的数据已经变了。这导致我们不得不做些别扭的事。尤其是，它迫使我们把查询与报表展示耦合在一起，对吧？假设你的应用程序需要做决定：要在这个网页上促销或展示哪些实体。

cues.en: Do we ever, you know, do we send the query to find out what those entities are and then later send a query to, you know, gather
cues.zh: 我们真的会先发一次查询找出是哪些实体，稍后再发一次查询去收集……

cues.en: the data we need for display?
cues.zh: ……展示所需的数据吗？

cues.en: No. A lot of times we piggyback those two things together because we're afraid of the result sets not matching up anymore. That's actually a fear that's born of the lack of basis again,
cues.zh: 不会。很多时候我们把这两件事顺带绑在一起做，因为担心两次的结果集对不上了。这种担忧其实又是源于缺乏一致的基准，

cues.en: and it's the biggest problem with round trips.
cues.zh: 而这正是网络往返最大的问题。

cues.en: And of course from a design perspective we know those two pieces of logic should be separate, they should be independent decisions. One part of my app knows the logic for deciding what should be displayed and the other one knows about what does the screen look like and what do we want to show on it.
cues.zh: 当然，从架构设计来看，我们知道这两块逻辑本该解耦，它们应该是独立的决策。应用程序的一部分负责决定该展示什么的业务逻辑，另一部分则负责页面长什么样、以及要在上面呈现什么内容。

cues.en: We have problems related to consistency and scale. I don't know if anybody saw any of the NoSQL talks,
cues.zh: 我们面临一致性和规模方面的问题。不知道有没有人听过那些NoSQL的演讲，

cues.en: this week, but you know, a lot of times we have difficulty scaling
cues.zh: 这周，但你知道，很多时候我们在扩展方面遇到困难

cues.en: servers that are
cues.zh: 服务器是……

cues.en: monolithic by default
cues.zh: 默认单体式

cues.en: And, you know, we've seen NoSQL, we've seen the Dynamo paper and some of these other technologies, and I think one of the questions we have in revisiting the architecture of a database is what's possible,
cues.zh: 你知道，我们见证了 NoSQL，见证了 Dynamo 论文和其他一些技术，我认为在重新审视数据库架构时，我们面临的问题之一就是什么是可能的，

cues.en: right? How much of the value propositions of databases can we retain
cues.zh: 对吧？我们能在多大程度上保留数据库的价值主张

cues.en: while tapping into some of the new value propositions of distributed systems, in particular their arbitrary scalability
cues.zh: 同时利用分布式系统的一些新价值主张，特别是其任意可扩展性

cues.en: and elasticity.
cues.zh: 以及弹性。

cues.en: Also I think people are sort of adopting
cues.zh: 我也觉得大家正在慢慢接受

cues.en: these distributed systems
cues.zh: 这些分布式系统

cues.en: and getting a bunch of complexity as a result because they're trading off
cues.zh: 结果就带来了一大堆复杂度，因为他们在做权衡

cues.en: distribution and scale for consistency,
cues.zh: 分发和规模确保一致性，

cues.en: they're losing consistency in
cues.zh: 他们正在失去一致性

cues.en: the trade off.
cues.zh: 权衡。

cues.en: But we have things like Dynamo and Bigtable, how do we use them?
cues.zh: 但我们有Dynamo和Bigtable这样的东西，该怎么用它们呢？

cues.en: Other problems we have in general when we talk about traditional databases are flexibility problems.
cues.zh: 当我们谈论传统数据库时，通常还会遇到灵活性问题。

cues.en: You know, everybody knows the rigidity of relational databases and the big rectangles and, you know, the the
cues.zh: 大家都知道关系型数据库很死板，那些大矩形，还有那个

cues.en: artifice you have in having to form intersection record tables and things like that.
cues.zh: 你不得不构建交集记录表之类东西的那种技巧。

cues.en: Things that you really shouldn't have to know about, and your application ends up
cues.zh: 有些东西你本不该操心，但你的应用最终还是会牵扯到

cues.en: becoming
cues.zh: 成为

cues.en: rigid because it does know about those.
cues.zh: 它之所以死板，是因为它确实了解那些东西。

cues.en: In addition, lots of things are difficult to represent in a traditional relational model like sparse data or irregular data, hierarchical data,
cues.zh: 此外，很多东西很难用传统的关系模型来表示，比如稀疏数据或不规则数据、层级数据，

cues.en: and things like that. So we want to be more flexible. We want to be more agile in our development,
cues.zh: 诸如此类。所以我们希望更灵活，希望开发更敏捷，

cues.en: and we want to try to avoid this rigidity
cues.zh: 并且希望尽量避免这种僵化

cues.en: seeping in.
cues.zh: 渗入进来。

cues.en: And of course, again, to the talk earlier, another thing we want to try to get right if we revisit database architecture
cues.zh: 当然，回到之前那场演讲，如果我们重新审视数据库架构，还有一件事我们想做好，

cues.en: is information and time. In particular, we want a database,
cues.zh: 那就是信息与时间。特别是，我们想要一个数据库，

cues.en: that we can use to represent information, we can use to obtain
cues.zh: 能用来表示信息，能用来获取

cues.en: real memory and real record keeping like we used to have before we had computers.
cues.zh: 真实的记忆和真实的记录保存，就像我们在有计算机之前那样。

cues.en: And there's lots of good reasons for this. It helps support decision making, as I said in my talk before,
cues.zh: 这有很多充分的理由。正如我之前演讲中所说，它有助于支持决策，

cues.en: and auditing,
cues.zh: 以及审计，

cues.en: and there's plenty of domains in which it's a requirement and people are doing this manually on top of systems that don't really understand that that's what you're trying to do. I mean how many people have ever added timestamp field themselves to tables and managed it all themselves?
cues.zh: 而且有很多领域这是硬性要求，人们正在那些并不真正理解你想做什么的系统上手动完成这件事。我的意思是，有多少人曾经自己往表里加时间戳字段，全靠自己管理？

cues.en: People have, right? How many people have written a query that gets you now out of that table?
cues.zh: 有人干过，对吧？有多少人写过从那张表里取出“现在”的查询？

cues.en: Yeah, how many people have tuned that?
cues.zh: 对，有多少人优化过那个查询？

cues.en: Yeah, that's a nightmare. Anybody like that query? Tuning that query? It was brutal,
cues.zh: 对，那简直是噩梦。有人喜欢那个查询吗？优化它？太折磨人了，

cues.en: right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: The contention is terrible, especially if
cues.zh: 争用非常糟糕，特别是如果

cues.en: also an online system.
cues.zh: 它还是一个在线系统。

cues.en: And the last thing I think we'd like from databases
cues.zh: 我觉得我们想从数据库里得到的最后一样东西

cues.en: that maybe we don't think about now because
cues.zh: 也许现在没考虑过，因为

cues.en: we don't connect the two necessarily,
cues.zh: 我们不一定把这两者联系起来，

cues.en: I think is strong model for perception and reaction.
cues.zh: 我认为是用于感知和反应的强模型。

cues.en: Right? Perception is part of what I was talking about before, getting that stable basis for decision making. Reaction is more like eventing,
cues.zh: 对吧？感知是我之前谈过的一部分，就是获得稳定的决策基础。反应更像是事件处理，

cues.en: right? Things are changing in the world. How do we see change in a traditional client server database?
cues.zh: 对吧？世界在变化。在传统客户端服务器数据库里，我们怎么看到变化？

cues.en: What do we do?
cues.zh: 我们怎么做？

cues.en: It's the big four letter word, begins with P and ends with OLL.
cues.zh: 就是那个以P开头、以OLL结尾的四字母词。

cues.en: Poll. We poll.
cues.zh: 轮询。我们轮询。

cues.en: Very gross, right? So we'd like to be able to make reactive systems that don't poll.
cues.zh: 非常糟糕，对吧？所以我们希望能构建不轮询的反应式系统。

cues.en: And we'd like those systems to get consistent views of the world, which is another difficult thing. Even if you build
cues.zh: 我们还希望这些系统能获得一致的世界视图，这又是另一件难事。即使你

cues.en: manually, say a trigger based eventing system, right? People have done that, right? So triggers and they say, oh, something changed. It's like, okay, great. Well, in between when they told you something changed,
cues.zh: 手动构建，比如基于触发器的事件系统，对吧？人们做过这个，对吧？触发器说，哦，有东西变了。好，很好。但在他们告诉你东西变了之后，

cues.en: and you're wanting to make a decision on the basis of it, maybe you're going go back to the database, what's the basis now for that? Did it change again between when you, you know, what's in flight? You have no way to know
cues.zh: 到你想基于此做决策之间，也许你会回到数据库，那现在的依据是什么？在你操作期间它又变了吗？你根本没法知道

cues.en: this changed and that change was related to the database at this point in time, and you can go back and ask questions to figure out what was going on and what either caused that change or what the effects of that change should be, or how it relates to the rest of the world, you have no way to do that. You just were told something changed and maybe you value about it, but not where that's situated relative to the rest of the world. So we want to do that better.
cues.zh: 这个变了，那个变化在此时与数据库相关，你可以回去提问，弄清楚发生了什么、是什么导致了这个变化、或者这个变化应该有什么效果、或者它和世界其他地方有什么关系，你没法做到。你只是被告知有东西变了，也许你关心它，但不知道它相对于世界其他地方处于什么位置。所以我们想做得更好。

cues.en: So if we're going to take a database apart, we have to look at how it's put together.
cues.zh: 所以如果要拆解一个数据库，就得先看看它是怎么组装起来的。

cues.en: And this is just, this is not a particular database we're talking about here. This should be familiar though to anybody who's dealt with traditional databases and how they're laid out. I'm sorry, this font is too small.
cues.zh: 这里说的并不是某个特定的数据库。不过，任何接触过传统数据库、了解它们结构的人应该都对此很熟悉。抱歉，这个字体太小了。

cues.en: And the guts, the meat of it is at the bottom, so we'll start at the bottom. A
cues.zh: 核心和精髓在底部，所以我们从底部开始讲。

cues.en: database
cues.zh: 数据库

cues.en: certainly is something in general we expect to be durable.
cues.zh: 通常来说，我们期望它是持久可靠的。

cues.en: So most of the traditional databases are built around, there is this disk,
cues.zh: 所以大多数传统数据库的构建都围绕磁盘展开，

cues.en: and we're going to put that disk in a box and that box is going to be in charge of the disk,
cues.zh: 我们把磁盘放进一个盒子里，由这个盒子来管理磁盘，

cues.en: and everything comes from there. So there's some IO subsystem
cues.zh: 一切都从那里来。所以会有一个 IO 子系统

cues.en: that deals with the disk,
cues.zh: 负责处理磁盘，

cues.en: right, and then there's sort of three fundamental,
cues.zh: 然后数据库会提供大致三种基础服务，

cues.zh: 我们面临的另一个问题是，如何表示变化？我们说过要累积事实，那么

cues.zh: 变化的粒度是什么？对吧？我们习惯于说更新这个位置，这里是位置的地址，或者这里是位置的主键，你知道，去那里做点什么。

cues.zh: 如果我们不想再那样说了，

cues.zh: 如果我们只想累积事实，那么什么是根本的

cues.zh: 新颖性单元？你知道，我有一个新客户，我要对数据库说什么？

cues.zh: 我们要说的是，在最底层

cues.en: we can represent this process, right? So this is the problem we're trying to solve, right? The novelty problem. We're going to say we can represent novelty by just as assertions or retractions of facts,
cues.zh: 我们可以表示这个过程，对吧？这就是我们要解决的问题，对吧？新颖性问题。我们要说，我们可以用事实的断言或撤回来表示新颖性，

cues.en: right? This new thing is true. This new thing is true. That thing that was true is not true anymore.
cues.zh: 对吧？这个新事物是真的。这个新事物是真的。那个曾经为真的事不再为真了。

cues.en: Okay? Still a fact that it was true. From then to here,
cues.zh: 明白吗？它曾经为真仍然是个事实。从那时到这里，

cues.en: it was true.
cues.zh: 它曾为真。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: this ends up being the minimal possible representation of process.
cues.zh: 这最终成为过程的最小可能表示。

cues.en: Right? With this you can build,
cues.zh: 对吧？有了这个你就能构建，

cues.en: you can express anything in these terms. And so we'll say that all the other transformations
cues.zh: 你可以用这些术语表达任何东西。所以我们会说，所有其他变换

cues.en: will expand into this.
cues.zh: 都会展开成这个。

cues.en: And I'll show you that a little bit later.
cues.zh: 稍后我会给你们展示这一点。

cues.en: The other key thing we want to do with processes is we want to reify it. How many people have heard of like event sourcing or anything like that? So one of the ideas behind it is that
cues.zh: 关于过程，我们想做的另一件关键事情是把它具体化。有多少人听说过事件溯源之类的？所以它背后的一个理念是，

cues.en: if you talk about a database and you just look at a database,
cues.zh: 如果你谈论一个数据库，你只是看着一个数据库，

cues.en: that's been running for a while, that's had a lot of activity. When you look at it and you want to know what happened, how do you figure that out?
cues.zh: 它已经运行了一段时间，有过大量活动。当你看着它，想知道发生了什么，你怎么弄清楚？

cues.en: How did become
cues.zh: 它是怎么变成

cues.en: what it is?
cues.zh: 现在这个样子的？

cues.en: You have no resources for doing that, right? Unless you know how to read the logs, right? Maybe there's a transaction log and maybe there's a way to read that. But a lot of times you're going have to sort of replay that because that's just a recessive, that's just a successive
cues.zh: 你没有任何资源来做这件事，对吧？除非你知道怎么读日志，对吧？也许有个事务日志，也许有办法读取它。但很多时候你得某种程度上重放它，因为那只是一系列递进的

cues.en: set of modifications to places. It was really hard to read that and understand what happened. If instead we say we're going to reify process. When you add a new customer, there's going to be something that says there is a new customer, that customer's name is Sally.
cues.zh: 对位置的修改。要读懂它并理解发生了什么真的很难。相反，如果我们说我们要把过程具体化。当你添加一个新客户时，会有某个东西说有一个新客户，那个客户的名字是 Sally。

cues.en: That's what's going to be in a reified version
cues.zh: 这就是具体化版本中会有的内容

cues.en: of process that says process is just assertions and retractions of facts. So that's great, so we want to make a thing out of that because that's something that we can store, we can look at, we can understand when we look at it. This, this is the, this change happened. We added this, we retracted that email, we added a new email, we sold this.
cues.zh: 对过程的表述：过程不过是对事实的断言和撤回。这很好，所以我们要把它做成实体，因为这样我们就能存储它、查看它、理解它。看这里，这个变化发生了。我们添加了这个，撤回了那封邮件，添加了新邮件，卖掉了这个。

cues.en: We did this, we did this. Fact, fact, fact, fact, fact. These things happened, right? It's an information system. Fact, fact, fact, fact, fact.
cues.zh: 我们做了这个，做了那个。事实、事实、事实、事实、事实。这些事都发生了，对吧？这是一个信息系统。事实、事实、事实、事实、事实。

cues.en: That's going to be great because that's going let us do some other cool things later like events.
cues.zh: 这将会很棒，因为它让我们以后能做其他酷炫的事情，比如事件。

cues.zh: 增量累积过程。其中一件

cues.zh: 需要

cues.zh: 理解的重要事情是，它确实是添加到

cues.zh: 已有的内容之上。

cues.zh: 所以这意味着，如果你在任何时间点查看数据库的视图，

cues.zh: 你都能访问仍然存在于内部的过去，就像树木的内层年轮依然存在一样。它不是那种上周二一个快照、周三一个、周四一个、周五一个，每个

cues.en: has more stuff in it.
cues.zh: 都包含更多内容。

cues.en: It's as if any time you look at the database, it includes all of history inside of it. And this is important for an information model where we want to give people decision making capabilities that say, how much have things changed in this window of time or count
cues.zh: 就好像你任何时候查看数据库，它都包含了内部的所有历史。这对于信息模型很重要，我们希望赋予人们决策能力，比如在这个时间窗口内变化了多少，或者统计

cues.en: how many of those that happened over a window of time. We need all the time in one place, we don't want a bunch of independent records, Here's Tuesdays, facts on Wednesdays and Thursdays separately.
cues.zh: 在这段时间窗口内发生了多少。我们需要所有时间都集中在一处，而不是一堆独立的记录——这是周二的事实，周三和周四的分开存放。

cues.en: So we have this growing tree ring thing.
cues.zh: 于是我们就有了这个不断生长的年轮结构。

cues.en: Alright, so that's our plan.
cues.zh: 好，这就是我们的计划。

cues.en: How do we do it? We're talking more now at the
cues.zh: 我们怎么做呢？我们现在更多地是在

cues.en: at the model level, right, we want to deconstruct this.
cues.zh: 在模型层面上，对吧，我们想对此进行解构。

cues.en: Now we're looking at just the server component, right, indexing, transactions, query, IO, and disk.
cues.zh: 现在只看服务端组件，对吧，索引、事务、查询、IO 和磁盘。

cues.en: And I think you can divide this up into halves,
cues.zh: 我觉得你可以把它分成两半，

cues.en: right, and this is what I said before, we want to separate process
cues.zh: 对，这就是我之前说的，我们想把进程分开

cues.en: from perception,
cues.zh: 从感知角度来看，

cues.en: right? Because there's a process part of this, right? Novelty processing.
cues.zh: 对吧？因为这里面有个过程的部分，对吧？新颖性处理。

cues.en: I have a new thing, it has to go through a transaction processing thing, maybe indexing happens on it then or not, don't know, it's an open question at this point in the talk. And then there's output to the storage system,
cues.zh: 我有了一个新东西，它要经过一个事务处理环节，也许之后会对它做索引，也许不会，不知道，在演讲的这个阶段这还是个开放问题。然后会输出到存储系统，

cues.zh: 完全正确。

cues.en: independent of that is a perception characteristic to the use of databases, right? I have a question, I want to ask the question, maybe that leverages indexes,
cues.zh: 与此无关的是，使用数据库有一种典型的认知，对吧？我有个问题，我想问这个问题，也许是利用索引的那个问题，

cues.en: almost definitely it does.
cues.zh: 几乎可以肯定是的。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 还有

cues.en: there's going to be input. This is all process relative, input to me, right, as I read back from storage.
cues.zh: 会有输入。这些都是相对于进程的，对我来说是输入，对吧，当我从存储中读回时。

cues.en: We can separate these two things out.
cues.zh: 我们可以把这两件事分开处理。

cues.en: And we can only because we've adopted an information model and immutability.
cues.zh: 而我们之所以能做到，是因为采用了信息模型和不可变性。

cues.en: So the model we're trying to get to, and again this is not yet a physical model, is one where we can empower
cues.zh: 我们要努力达到的模型——再次强调，这还不是一个物理模型——是那种我们能够赋能的模型

cues.en: applications,
cues.zh: 应用程序，

cues.en: and you can read this as application servers or analytics servers or anything you want, it's not like a desktop application,
cues.zh: 你可以把它理解为应用服务器、分析服务器，或者任何你想要的东西，它不像桌面应用程序，

cues.en: right? We want to empower
cues.zh: 对吧？我们想赋能

cues.en: independent
cues.zh: 独立的

cues.en: applications
cues.zh: 应用程序

cues.en: with as much of these capabilities as we can. We want them to be able to perceive change, we want them to be able to react to it, we want them to be able to independently remember anything that's important to their decision making process. And we want them to make decisions
cues.zh: 我们希望尽可能多地具备这些能力。我们希望它们能够感知变化，能够对变化做出反应，能够独立记住任何对其决策过程重要的信息。并且我们希望它们做出决策

cues.en: and then possibly
cues.zh: 然后可能

cues.en: affect
cues.zh: 影响

cues.en: the process that they're sharing. What we want to do, and obviously there's going to be some
cues.zh: 他们正在共享的进程。我们想要做的，而且显然会有一些

cues.en: shared resources here, right? There's got to be some coordination around
cues.zh: 这里的共享资源，对吧？肯定需要围绕它进行一些协调

cues.en: change,
cues.zh: 改变，

cues.en: right? And there's going have to be some shared resource around storage.
cues.zh: 对吧？而且在存储方面肯定需要某种共享资源。

cues.en: We want to minimize
cues.zh: 我们要尽量减少

cues.en: the coordination that's
cues.zh: 支持这一点所需的

cues.en: necessary to support this. But that's the model we want. Because now if we can do this, if we want a more powerful system, what do we have to do?
cues.zh: 协调开销。但这正是我们想要的模型。因为现在如果我们能做到这一点，如果想要更强大的系统，我们需要做什么？

cues.en: If we want more query capability,
cues.zh: 如果我们想要更强的查询能力，

cues.en: what do we need to do?
cues.zh: 我们需要做什么？

cues.en: Just add more of these guys. We don't really care about this growing because we're not asking it to do much, just some coordination.
cues.zh: 只需增加更多这样的节点。我们不太关心它的增长，因为我们并不要求它做太多事，只是一些协调工作。

cues.en: So if we revisit that whole tree ring thing, now we're into implementation details,
cues.zh: 所以如果我们重新审视整个树环结构，现在进入实现细节，

cues.en: how do we represent state? How do we represent this immutable
cues.zh: 如何表示状态？如何表示这个不可变的

cues.en: expanding value?
cues.zh: 不断扩展的值？

cues.en: Right? We know one thing, whatever representation we use, it has to be organized to support query,
cues.zh: 对吧？我们知道一件事：无论用什么表示方式，都必须组织好以支持查询，

cues.en: right? It has to be sorted in some way. That's, that's really sort of the fundamental leverage capability we have is sorting things.
cues.zh: 对吧？它必须以某种方式排序。这其实是我们拥有的根本性杠杆能力——对事物进行排序。

cues.en: And it ends up that there's a technique that can be used, you know, it's used in functional programming quite often,
cues.zh: 结果发现有一种技术可以使用，你知道，它在函数式编程中经常被用到，

cues.en: called persistent data structures. And the word persistent there does not mean durable.
cues.zh: 叫做持久化数据结构。这里的“持久化”并不是指持久耐用。

cues.en: It's a different notion of persistence and it has to do with the fact that you can represent a large immutable structure. And it doesn't matter whether it's supposed to represent an array or
cues.zh: 它是一种不同的持久性概念，与这样一个事实有关：你可以表示一个大型的不可变结构。无论它是用来表示数组还是

cues.en: map,
cues.zh: 映射，

cues.en: you can represent almost anything,
cues.zh: 你几乎可以表示任何东西，

cues.en: or sorted set would be another example we're going to use, as a tree.
cues.zh: 或者有序集合——这是我们接下来要用的另一个例子——都可以表示为一棵树。

cues.en: And you can represent
cues.zh: 你可以

cues.en: that immutably
cues.zh: 以不可变的方式

cues.en: by using something called structural sharing.
cues.zh: 通过一种叫做结构共享的技术来表示它。

cues.en: So this tree could represent anything. It could represent, for instance, a sorted set.
cues.zh: 这棵树可以代表任何东西。比如，它可以代表一个有序集合。

cues.en: And this is the view of it we have right now, and it contains all these nodes. If we want to add
cues.zh: 这就是我们当前看到的视图，它包含所有这些节点。如果我们想添加

cues.en: another
cues.zh: 另一个

cues.en: child
cues.zh: 子节点

cues.en: to this node, so we want to make a new version of the set, we don't want to update it in place,
cues.zh: 到这个节点，也就是想创建这个集合的新版本，而不想原地更新，

cues.en: we're going to need to allocate a new node for that leaf and then copy the path to the root.
cues.zh: 我们就需要为那个叶子节点分配一个新节点，然后复制到根节点的路径。

cues.en: Then we have a new tree
cues.zh: 然后我们得到一棵新树

cues.en: that has this new piece of information in it, and substantially
cues.zh: 其中包含这个新信息，并且大体上

cues.en: share structure with the old tree. And we can do that because why?
cues.zh: 与旧树共享结构。我们能做到这一点，为什么呢？

cues.en: It's all immutable.
cues.zh: 因为一切都是不可变的。

cues.en: So this is the underpinnings of what are called persistent data structures.
cues.zh: 这就是所谓持久化数据结构的底层基础。

cues.en: So we can do this in memory, and it's done in memory by most functional programming languages. What we're going to start to do though, is do this
cues.zh: 所以我们可以在内存中这样做，大多数函数式编程语言都是在内存中实现的。不过我们接下来要开始做的是，把这套机制

cues.en: on disk. So we'll have a really persistent, a persistent persistent, or I'd rather say durable persistent data structures
cues.zh: 放到磁盘上。这样我们就会有真正持久的、持久化的持久化，或者我更愿意说，耐久持久化数据结构

cues.en: that have this kind of shape.
cues.zh: 具有这种形态。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: you saw in the earlier diagram, right, we had a server and it had IO and a disk,
cues.zh: 你在之前的图里看到了，对吧，我们有一个服务器，它有 IO 和磁盘，

cues.en: right? I don't want to know about IOs and disks anymore.
cues.zh: 对吧？我不想再关心 IO 和磁盘了。

cues.en: There was a paper recently that came out, it said disk locality considered irrelevant,
cues.zh: 最近有一篇论文出来，说磁盘局部性被认为无关紧要，

cues.en: right? It's another one of these old notions
cues.zh: 对吧？这是又一个旧观念

cues.en: that's now
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: dying.
cues.zh: 正在消亡。

cues.en: It used to be, boy, if you're not the machine that has the discs,
cues.zh: 过去是这样的，天哪，如果你不是那台拥有磁盘的机器，

cues.en: you're at a tremendous disadvantage
cues.zh: 你在计算上就处于极大的劣势

cues.en: from a computational perspective.
cues.zh: 从计算的角度来看。

cues.en: Because that machine, it's got a card that's attached to the disk, it can get the data up into memory, it's lightning fast,
cues.zh: 因为那台机器有块卡连着磁盘，能把数据快速读进内存，速度飞快，

cues.en: that machine has privileged access to that disk. If you try to access that data on the disk from another machine, you're going be paying a huge overhead.
cues.zh: 那台机器对那块磁盘有特权访问。你要是想从另一台机器访问磁盘上的数据，开销会非常大。

cues.en: Well now, how much faster are networks?
cues.zh: 那么现在，网络快了多少？

cues.en: Way faster. And what's the differential between disk and memory?
cues.zh: 快得多。磁盘和内存之间的差距呢？

cues.en: Huge.
cues.zh: 巨大。

cues.en: It ends up that anybody that needs to access the disk is losing.
cues.zh: 结果就是，任何需要访问磁盘的人都在吃亏。

cues.en: And the guy who has the disk in the same box is only losing very, very slightly less than anybody else would lose. So it doesn't matter anymore.
cues.zh: 而磁盘就在同一台机器上的人，也只是比其他人少亏那么一点点。所以已经无所谓了。

cues.en: That kind of locality is not the way we should be architecting
cues.zh: 这种本地性不应该成为我们架构系统的方式

cues.en: systems. We don't care about it. We care a lot more about
cues.zh: 我们不在乎它。我们更关心的是

cues.zh: 把数据放进内存，并在这样做时保持良好的本地性。

cues.en: But if we actually have to touch the disk, we're losing anyway.
cues.zh: 但如果我们真得碰磁盘，那反正都是亏。

cues.en: So we're just going to wrap up both the IO and the disk and say that's something we're going to call a black box called storage.
cues.zh: 所以我们干脆把 IO 和磁盘都包起来，说这是我们称之为存储的黑盒。

cues.en: What we're going to put in storage
cues.zh: 我们要放进存储的

cues.en: are two things.
cues.zh: 是两样东西。

cues.zh: 一个是所有新事物的日志，来一个记一个。这其实是个追加型的活儿，对吧？有人说，我卖了这个，Sally

cues.zh: 给了我封邮件，事实、事实、事实。我们就尽可能快地把这些事实铲进存储。

cues.en: The other thing that will be in storage are much the same
cues.zh: 存储里另一类东西，形状和

cues.zh: 我们以前本地拥有的东西差不多，对吧？当我们有个单体数据库时，

cues.zh: 磁盘上有 B 树。

cues.en: We're now going to have those persistent trees in storage
cues.zh: 现在，我们要把这些持久化树放进存储里

cues.en: with nodes that we just don't change, but otherwise it's the same kind of idea. We've moved away from disk to storage
cues.zh: 节点我们不去修改，但整体思路是一样的。我们已经从磁盘转向了存储

cues.en: and we're storing
cues.zh: 并且我们存储的是

cues.en: index segments that we're not going to mutate.
cues.zh: 不会修改的索引段。

cues.en: But the key thing now is that we're treating
cues.zh: 但现在关键是，我们对待

cues.en: storage
cues.zh: 存储

cues.en: with

cues.zh: 那个查询对当前数据有效。我可以告诉数据库，把你自己截至上周的样子给我。我可以拿同一个查询，对那个数据库值运行。它不再按时间参数化了，对吧？数据库知道我在假装现在是上周。现在同一个查询你可以问，它没有任何时间，时间不是连接的一部分。

cues.zh: 对吧？它只从一个有效一致点移动到另一个有效一致点。中间永远没有过渡状态，没有重新协调

cues.zh: 然后你可以去看我当时看到的完全一样的东西，这样你就知道该做什么。

cues.zh: 因为我们把东西拆开了，就有自由重新安置它们。我们不在乎查询在哪里运行。不在乎存储在哪里。不在乎事务器在哪里运行。对于把东西放在哪里，你有很大的灵活性。你可以把数据放到 DynamoDB 上，把整个系统跑在你的局域网里，把 MAMcache 放在局域网里，把互联网其实可能在中间这件事隔离开来。
